answer.answer: The next non-profile work package should remove foreground `/in/playerActivity` cache-miss rebuilds. Separately, the raid profile route should render local raid results first and defer Bungie collectible enrichment and Pantheon loading.

claims.value: The highest-value non-profile target is the `/in/playerActivity` cache-miss path, especially its effect on analytics home. It combines high traffic with a severe slow tail: RUM recorded 13,210 calls over 7 days at avg 3.69 s, p75 1.09 s, and p95 12.03 s; APM recorded 23,255 `GET /in/playerActivity` spans at avg 1.99 s, p75 2 ms, and p95 13.03 s. The p75/p95 split is consistent with fast cache hits and expensive misses. The code path reads the `apiPlayerActivity` cache but falls back to `memcache.GetPlayerActivity`; meanwhile `sweeperbot.cachePlayerActivity` refreshes every 5 minutes with a matching 5 minute TTL, allowing foreground requests to pay for the Redis scan. Last-24-hour logs recorded 68 foreground rebuilds and 204 shard logs, with shard-scan p95 about 18 s and math p95 about 16 s. This target also sits in the heavily used analytics area: `analytics.home` had 16,389 canonical human pageviews over 7 days.

Recommended intervention: change `/in/playerActivity` to stale-while-revalidate. Retain a last-known-good result under a stale TTL longer than the 5 minute refresh interval; serve that stale value immediately when the fresh entry is absent or expired; permit only one locked background rebuild; and have `sweeperbot.cachePlayerActivity` refresh before fresh expiry. A web request should never run the Redis shard scan. If no last-known-good value exists, return an explicit unavailable/no-data response rather than rebuilding synchronously, matching the documented Discord behavior for a missing cache. This is a proposal from the saved evidence, not a verified implementation.

On `/p/:identifier/raids`, the bottleneck is Bungie collectible/profile enrichment rather than raid SQL or images. `loadLogbookRaidSources` waits for all concurrent sources, including `bungie.GetD2ProfileStats(..., bungie.ProfileWCollectibles)`, before responding; that Bungie result supplies raid exotic, armor, triumph, guardian-rank, and avatar enrichment. The same route immediately starts a separate Pantheon request that repeats `ProfileWCollectibles` before the Pantheon tab is opened. APM showed `GET /in/logbook/profile/:identifier/raids` at avg 1.81 s, p75 2.33 s, p95 3.77 s, while `source:bungieprofile,state:ok` averaged about 2.70 s with 95th about 3.77 s; the local raid sources were only milliseconds (`raiddifficultysummaries` about 2.7 ms, `raidcarries` about 6.1 ms average/10.1 ms 95th, and `raidseals` about 0.6 ms). Change the route to return and render the shell plus local clears/full clears/carries/fastest data first, then fetch collectible/progress enrichment separately. claims.value: Straylight is a user-owned, portable agent context and durable-work layer for agents: an agent-first durable machine-continuity product and protocol, distinct from Metis, the knowledge-base system. It is not primarily a notes app, wiki, synchronized folder, transcript archive, retrieval product, or memory database; full source and artifact access supports the work rather than defining retrieval as the product.

Beyond durable learned knowledge, Straylight must preserve the live state needed to resume and advance work: goals, current state, evidence, decisions, hypotheses, plans, artifacts, computations, unresolved or open questions, rejected paths or approaches, checkpoints, and resumable next actions. A later agent must be able to inspect how that state was reached, reopen and query it, compute over it, revise and verify it as evidence changes, checkpoint it, and leave a better durable handoff.

Obsidian is not the product boundary because Straylight's canonical interaction model is agent-first, not note-first. Metis and its Obsidian vault organize the human knowledge base and supply a representative prototype and evaluation corpus; Obsidian, Markdown, and human-readable notes are prototype inputs, human projections, and export formats. Raw Markdown is therefore neither assumed to be Straylight's only or canonical storage representation nor its truth boundary; the product is the portable agent context and durable-work layer designed over such corpora.

The completed first benchmark was too narrow because it evaluated retrieval readiness rather than the product's end-to-end continuation promise: it used 20 frozen questions and 53 gold evidence items, compared direct full-file access, one-shot BM25 top-k, and a minimal deterministic Memory Workspace, and exercised only `memory.open`, `memory.query`, and `memory.read`; model-directed `memory.compute` and `memory.verify`, checkpoint/revision behavior, and durable next-state production remained untested. Policy 0.2 reached 17 of 20 cases and 46 of 53 evidence items at P95 context of 11,999 characters, while one-shot top-k also reached 17 of 20, recovered 48 of 53, and used about 1,070 mean estimated tokens versus 2,932, so the workspace hypothesis was not demonstrated; policy 0.2 is only a regression baseline and its tuned score is not holdout evidence. The expanded gate must use an untouched holdout and compare direct filesystem tools, an agent-first workspace with model-directed `open`, `query`, `read`, `compute`, `verify`, checkpoint, and revision behavior, and fixed handoff/context packs. It must prove that a fresh agent can resume, iterate, verify, compute, and leave correct durable next-state artifacts on real workloads—Warmind/Charlemagne performance and incident work, StarRupture factory planning, Switzerland trip planning under changing constraints, and Straylight's own evolution—while preserving final-answer correctness and completeness, evidence-chain recall, temporal and supersession accuracy, contradiction handling, source fidelity, project continuation, and durable-state quality. Retrieval-only scores remain a regression lane, and no canonical storage-engine decision is justified until the blinded model-answer evaluation clears this gate.
